call.rationale: I re-underwrote the post-earnings review against fresh data and I am tightening the floor instead of exiting into strength. The fired review was correct yesterday — MU had beaten but the market sold it — yet today's tape has repaired that damage: price is back to about $1,097 on 1.83x average volume, sitting just under the $1,100 target area. This was not a clean new PEAD reset because the latest EPS beat was only 2.6%, below my 5% clean-signal threshold, so I am not treating this print as a fresh add. I am also not leaving the old $1,041 floor in place when the position is up more than 22% and the ladder health already flags the gain as under-protected. Invalidation check: the stock has not closed below the $969 stop-loss assumption; Q4 revenue did not miss the $50B guide — it beat at $54.23B — so that condition did not happen; and there is no evidence of a major HBM customer deferral or cancellation. What did happen is the drift matured and the stock is now back in the target zone, so the right move is to ratchet protection higher under the reclaimed breakout area and let the name either finish the last bit of upside or stop us out with a real gain.
call.structural_unchanged_reason: The core HBM-demand and earnings-upgrade belief still stands; this change is about protecting a mature PEAD winner whose latest print did not qualify as a fresh clean beat-and-raise signal.

thesis.convictionRationale: The regulatory environment is genuinely de-risked relative to the prior PASS: Lifyorli's FDA approval confirms the molecule works and that FDA will approve relacorilant when data supports it. The CRL was an efficacy-data request, the additional analyses were characterized as positive by management, and the resubmission is a Class 2 review — a narrower hurdle than a first-time binary. That said, efficacy-focused CRLs carry real second-CRL risk that I cannot quantify from the outside, and the $12.5B market cap means a bad outcome gaps 40–60% through any stop. Insider selling at scale and no open-market buying from insiders with the best NDA read is the signal I respect most. MEDIUM is honest here — the thesis is directionally right, but no priced plan exists until R/R clears 2:1 at a real technical stop.
thesis.variantView: Consensus treats this as a routine re-filing after an administrative CRL; I think the efficacy-data ask is meaningfully harder than market pricing implies — approval probability is real but closer to 60–65%, not the 80%+ the stock's valuation embeds, making the entry level and stop placement critical to any viable R/R.
